items.text: Fuj, kaj je spet s to usrano pozo misleca?
items.q: Hooman mocks a roommate sitting in a thinker's pose. Does this sound like crude dorm talk?
before: Nekaj časa ni prišel glas nikogar. Hooman je rekel:

items.text: Huh, poglejte – se kdo od vas spomni ene dobre stvari pri vašem Babi?
items.q: Maman challenges her children to name one good thing about their father. Does this question read correctly?
A roommate snaps back at Eskandar with a crude retort about sucking up. Does this sound natural?
before: – Le zakaj bi tele, kakršno si ti, sploh imelo Šajarianovo pesem na telefonu?

items.text: Nobeno ime ti ne pristoji, prekleto.
items.q: Eskandar gives up hunting for a nickname for Hooman and raises his voice. Does this sound natural?
before: Glas mu je narastel in rekel je:

items.text: Naša šola je na koncu. Zadnja hiša. Če delamo hrup, nas bo učitelj udaril po rokah z ravnilom.
items.q: A boy warns the little ones about the strict teacher. Does this sound like a child talking?
before: Ghassem je spet rekel kaj. Potem je rekel:

items.text: Dobro, igra z blatom je končana. Pripravljeni na tajno misijo.
items.q: A boy calls his little brothers from mud play to his pretend mission. Does this sound like a child playing?
before: Omid in jaz sva hodila za njim. Zelo mi je bilo všeč. Še bolj kot igra z blatom. Omid in jaz sva se igrala z blatom na dvorišču. Ghassem je vedno glasno zaklical:

items.text: Uh, vsakič, ko mu rečeš, naj nekaj prinese, ga tako strese, kot da ga je udaril tok.
items.q: Maman complains that her son jolts as if shocked whenever he is asked to fetch something. Does this sound natural?
She teases him by dropping in the English slang word 'sneaky'. Does it sound natural for a young woman to say this?
before: – Danes ste se sredi fakultete pogovarjale še z nekaj drugimi dekleti, slišal sem.

items.text: Kje na mojem vratu piše stopnica?
items.q: Farid complains that Sajad used his neck as a foothold to climb into the top bunk. Does this retort sound natural?
before: Trije so se smejali in Sajad je zapustil sobo. Nekaj časa je bilo slišati samo glasova Eskandarja in Meysama, vse dokler Faridov glas ni vzplaval, kot da se duši.
– Av, av. Orlov Pogled, vzemi nogo z mojega vratu.
– Oh, oprosti. Objektivno, skušam priti v svojo posteljo. Težko je.

items.text: Danes ne razpravljajte v sobi, iz športne vzgoje sem dobil dvanajst, živci so mi v kurcu, pa vas bom opsoval.
items.q: Hooman, in a foul mood after a bad grade, warns his roommates. Does this sound like how he would say it?

items.text: Posral si tisti občutek, ki sem ga lovil iz pesmi, s tistim svojim zajebanim glasom.
items.q: Hooman swears at a roommate for ruining a song's mood with his awful singing. Does this sound like crude dorm talk?

items.text: Veliko ljudi tukaj pade. Gredo levo.
items.q: A boy playing a mission game warns that many people fail at this point. Does it sound like a child talking?
before: Tega dela se nikoli nisem naučil. Vedno je rekel najpomembnejše ... nekaj ... misije. Potem je rekel:

items.text: Samo šalimo se, da se smejemo, Nana-pesar-jan. Bi šel? Če bi šel, bi bila moja srčna želja.
items.q: Maman says they are only joking, and if her husband ever left, it would answer her prayers. Does this sound like her?

items.text: Jaz sem služabnik Starešine Krčme, čigar milost ...
items.q: Hooman opens Hafez at random for a fortune and reads this line. Does it read as classic poetry?
before: Hooman je odprl knjigo in rekel:

items.text: Pri novoletni sofri, ko sem bral pesem za mamo, je Maman namesto da bi bila vesela postala zaskrbljena.
items.q: He read his poem to his mother at the very moment the year turned at Norouz. Does this line make that moment clear?
